text: This is the final lesson of Chapter Two. You'll learn the OUTPUT clause, which lets a write statement return the rows it just affected.

SELECT always returns the rows it reads, but INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE normally just report how many rows were affected. OUTPUT closes that gap. Here, inserting a new row also immediately returns its generated ProductID, name, and price -- no separate SCOPE_IDENTITY call needed.

OUTPUT reads from two special pseudo-tables: inserted, holding new values, and deleted, holding old values. An UPDATE can reference both at once, because every changed row has a value before the update and a value after it.

A DELETE only ever has old values, so its OUTPUT clause can only reference deleted. This gives you permanent proof of exactly which rows were removed and what they contained, right in the same statement.

Add INTO to send the OUTPUT rows into a real table instead of just displaying them. Here, every row this DELETE removes is simultaneously inserted into an archive table, giving you a permanent record without writing a second statement.
That completes Chapter Two, Writing Data. Next, Chapter Three begins with the WHERE clause, where you'll go deeper on filtering and sorting the data you read.
